prize_parts.citation: For the experimental discovery of the Higgs boson with the ATLAS and CMS detectors at the Large Hadron Collider

statement.case_for: The 2012 observation of a 125 GeV boson by two independent experiments is the clearest clue from nature that physics has produced in a generation. The 2013 prize honoured the mechanism, and the experimental discovery that vindicated it has never been recognised. The result is mature (coupling measurements through Run 2 and Run 3 agree with the Standard Model), the interpretation is stable, and it settled the central open question of the Standard Model. After reading my colleagues' ballots I move one name in my attribution: Virdee should be in the trio. Lindroth and Pearce both reach for him independently, and a prize built only from ATLAS-side names plus Della Negra would look lopsided. Gianotti (ATLAS spokesperson at the announcement), Jenni (ATLAS founding spokesperson) and Virdee (CMS) give a balanced configuration, although Della Negra's claim for CMS is equally strong.
statement.case_against: Three names cannot represent two collaborations of thousands, and any trio omits someone with a serious claim, in particular Della Negra, who is excluded only by the three-person limit. The 2013 prize may also be argued to have discharged the committee's duty on the Higgs, and one could say the discovery's credit belongs to the machine and the collaborations rather than to individuals. Several colleagues (Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson) rank B012 higher, and the optical lattice clock case is cleaner in attribution (two names, no collaboration problem) and equally mature. If the committee decides that the attribution to individuals is not defensible for the Higgs experiments, B012 is the configuration I could support most readily.

responses.point: Pearce ranks IceCube first as an instrument-driven opening of a new window, and puts the Higgs experiments seventh because the 2013 prize may already have discharged the committee's duty on the Higgs.
responses.response: I agree on IceCube as a serious candidate and put it second myself; the diffuse flux is firm, and I value the observational clarity. But I disagree that 2013 discharged the Higgs. That prize recognised the theoretical mechanism, and the experimental discovery has no prize of its own; our process is about identifying the discovery first and the people second. The same logic argues for waiting on IceCube: only a few source associations (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, the Galactic plane) sit at modest significance, so the astrophysical interpretation is still developing, whereas the Higgs result has been confirmed by two experiments and measured in detail for more than a decade.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks optical lattice clocks first, citing the Katori magic-wavelength idea and Ye's drive to 10^-18 as a case where theory and experiment agree quantitatively and which opens new questions about time and gravity. She also puts the Higgs experiments third, naming Gianotti and Virdee as the most natural names.
responses.response: I accept her point on maturity and on the clean attribution: Katori and Ye is the tidiest pair on the list, and several independent laboratories have reproduced the 10^-18 level. I ranked it seventh because the fundamental-physics payoff (varying constants, dark matter, a redshift test at millimetre scale) is still prospective, and I want a clue from nature rather than a better ruler. I take her suggestion on Virdee and will put him in my trio. I would ask her to say more about how this prize is separate from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes before the committee commits.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks the Kane-Mele-Molenkamp topological insulator first, as a clear, mature prediction-plus-experiment case that continues the 2016 prize in a distinct direction.
responses.response: I agree it is mature and conceptually elegant, and the theory-experiment match is quantitative. My reservation, which he flags himself, is attribution: the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal for HgTe falls outside the credited names, and Zhang's death rules out a fair completion, so the Molenkamp part of the prize rests on an experiment whose guiding prediction is credited elsewhere. I also see the 2D-versus-3D question as unresolved. I do not think that is fatal, but it makes B018 less clean than the support it has received suggests, and I would want expert input on the HgTe priority before treating it as a front-runner.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene first as a simple mechanism in which band flattening opens a new field, with theory and experiment meeting.
responses.response: The Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction followed by correlated insulators and superconductivity is an attractive case, and I like the theory-meets-experiment structure. But I would hold back for a few more years: the pairing mechanism is not settled, the early experimental credit extends to Yuan Cao and others outside the list, and the Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto work complicates priority. By his own admission the interpretation is still debated. I am not saying it will not be a prize, only that the verdict from nature is less complete than for the Higgs or the clocks.

uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to honour the Higgs discovery through individual spokespersons and founders, or through the accelerator and detector builders (the LHC itself, B008, is not on the shortlist).
Which three of Gianotti, Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee best represent ATLAS and CMS; I would want the external expert reports on this point.
Whether the Higgs discovery's attribution problem is serious enough that the committee should prefer a two-name prize such as B012 or B013.
Whether the first prospective results from the optical clocks (variation of constants, redshift tests) will change the weighting of B012 over the next few years.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. My ties are to David Gross (PhD supervisor), Hector Rubinstein, Thomas Van Riet and the Uppsala string-theory group, and none of them is connected to any shortlisted candidate. My own research on dark bubble cosmology and horizonless black-hole mimickers touches B027 only indirectly, and B027 is not in my preferred configuration.
